article_sentences: The Court also asked the Union to clear the ambiguities in the pension rules.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) has upheld the grant of a War Injury pension to ex-armed forces personnel for the ailment which developed owing to his posting at Kargil as part of Operation Rakshak.

A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe dismissed the Union government's appeal against the High Court's and Armed Forces Tribunal's order which granted a War Injury pension to the ex-personnel in place of the disability pension.

At the same time, the Court also suggested that the government issue a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services of ex-personnel who became eligible for a War Injury Pension, noting that there is uncertainty about which Rules, Regulations, Instructions and Policies of the Ministry of Defence (MoD) are applicable.
“We continue to wonder why this uncertainty about applicable rules continues.
It is high time that the MoD issues a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services.
This is necessary for fairness in action and also for good governance.”, the Court said.
The respondent Narender Kumar joined the Indian Army in December 1996 and was posted at Kargil from July 2003 to July 2005.
During this posting, he was diagnosed with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in January 2005.
He was subsequently diagnosed with two spinal conditions while posted in West Bengal.
When he was discharged from service in January 2013, the Release Medical Board assessed his disabilities as aggravated by military service at 70%, rounded off to 75% for life.
He was granted disability pension comprising service and disability elements.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc at Odalarevu fishing villager, over 100 boats destroyed
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc at Odalarevu fishing villager, over 100 boats destroyed
stories.summary: Nearly one hundred boats have broken, another hundred more boats were scattered and dozens of boats were sunk in the backwaters near the confluence of Godavari river into the sea after cyclone Arnab made its landfall near Odalarevu village
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Following the landfall of Cyclone Arnab, the coastal village of Odalarevu faced near the confluence point where the Vynateya branch of the Godavari River meets the Bay of Bengal faced severe devastation as violent winds and surging backwaters swept away and destroyed a large number of fishing boats anchored along the riverbanks.
Fishermen and their families scrambled to recover their boats, engines and equipment from the water.
Women joined the men in the recovery efforts.

Wading through neck-deep water and harsh weather conditions, they spent hours cutting through the tangled fishing nets and pulling their boats out of the water as they tried to salvage whatever they could.
Of the approximately 300 boats anchored at the Odalarevu fish landing centre, over 100 were broken into pieces, while nearly 100 others were scattered along the riverbanks or submerged under water.
Individual families reported losing boats worth over ₹3 lakh each.
Additionally, specialised nets used to catch prawn, pomfret (chanduva), and tuna were damaged beyond repair after becoming entangled in the wreckage.
Local residents said that instead of catching fish to earn a living, families were forced to spend hours searching for their destroyed boats from the water.
The cyclone’s impact was equally severe onshore.
Dozens of coconut trees were uprooted across Odalarevu, blocking roads and snapping power lines, leaving the village without electricity.
Local residents estimate the total damage to exceed ₹3 crore, and fear it could take up to a year for the fishing community to fully recover.

He also urged the Union government to continue providing support through the NDRF and other central agencies for relief and rehabilitation.

stories.headline: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 28: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him. Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it's not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel. Netanyahu seeks to remain the country's longest-serving prime minister. In defiant comments after the vote, he dismissed the idea of partnering with Arab parties — whose constituents make up 20 per cent of Israel's population — as treasonous. On Wednesday, Netanyahu warned against a “dangerous government” that might include them. He won't work with the Arab-led parties, and they have ruled that out, too. His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group. But it's not clear whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office. Israeli voters choose parties, not individuals. With 85 per cent of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8 per cent and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1 per cent. The official count does not indicate how many seats each will have in parliament, the 120-seat Knesset. Emerging results indicated that neither Netanyahu's nor Eisenkot's coalition blocs would reach the 61 seats needed for a majority. Likud's vote share declined from 23.4 per cent in the previous election in 2022. Netanyahu faces a setback but not outright defeat Nearly 78 per cent of eligible voters turned out, the highest since 1999. Final results are expected in the coming days, including from hundreds of thousands of absentee ballots yet to be counted from military personnel and diplomats. Voting reflected unease over Netanyahu's alliance with the far-right and anger in a war-weary nation over military draft exemptions for the significant ultra-Orthodox Jewish population. But results suggest opponents were unable to capitalise on the grief caused by the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack to decisively push him from office. One partner losing support, however, was far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. For many Israelis, he represented the worst strain of Netanyahu's government, openly taunting Palestinian detainees and asserting that many in Gaza are “not even people.” Vote-counting suggested Likud would remain the largest party and best placed to be tapped to form a government by Israel's president, Isaac Herzog. The president, however, isn't required to task the leader of the party holding the most seats. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said Wednesday. The most obvious path to a parliamentary majority could involve Eisenkot partnering with Arab-led parties — which have 14.9 per cent of the votes counted — but that's politically challenging. In a speech early Wednesday that focused on national unity, Eisenkot pledged to form a government and promised “a new era — an era of hope." If no one can put together a majority coalition, new elections could be held early next year. Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate. Whether thousands of Israelis living abroad would again fly back home to vote, and whether Arab voters would again surge to the polls, is unclear. Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has announced the decision to reschedul polling and counting for the MPTC and ZPTC elections, amid the shortage of police personnel and polling staff.
The polling, which is supposed to be held on 3 November, will now be held on 5 November from 7am to 5pm.
Re-polling, if required, will be held on 6 November.
Meanwhile, counting has been postponed from 5 November to 7 November and will begin at 8am, with results to be declared as soon as counting is complete.

article_sentences: Former Supreme Court judge Abhay S. Oka on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said the roster system followed by the Supreme Court needs to be overhauled to bring greater transparency to the allocation of cases and eliminate the scope for “manual intervention” in their listing.

Mr. Oka pointed out that several Benches of the Supreme Court are assigned the same categories of cases under the roster, making it difficult for a litigant to know which Bench a freshly instituted case would eventually be listed before.
The practice, he said, left room for human intervention in deciding where a case would be listed.
“The object of a roster is to ensure that the possibility of manual intervention in listing is ruled out.
But when the same subject is assigned to multiple Benches, a case can possibly go to five different Benches.
Who then decides which Bench a freshly filed petition goes before — the Chief Justice of India or an official in the Registry?
The fact remains that there is manual intervention in the listing of cases,” he said.

Mr. Oka was delivering the keynote lecture at an event on the “Accountability of Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts” organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms (CJAR) in New Delhi.
The Chief Justice of India (CJI), as the “master of the roster”, has the administrative authority to constitute Benches and allocate judicial work among them.
Mr. Oka, however, said that the present system made the Supreme Court overly dependent on the office of the Chief Justice in matters of listing and allocation.
“The Supreme Court is too much of a Chief Justice-centric court.
The Supreme Court will become more favourable to litigants if it introduces a proper roster on a par with the High Courts, so that manual intervention by the CJI is ruled out,” he said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has stayed a Punjab and Haryana High Court order restraining judicial officers in Rohtak Sessions Division from entertaining bail applications in a case involving an alleged large-scale real estate investment scam in which investors were allegedly cheated of crores of rupees.
A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran passed the order on October 27 while hearing a special leave petition filed challenging the High Court's September 30 order.
The Court issued notice, returnable in four weeks, and stayed the operation of the impugned order in the meantime.
“Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.
Dasti service, in addition, is permitted.
In the meantime, there shall be stay of operation of the impugned order dated 30.09.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CRM M-42815/2026”, the Court ordered.

The High Court had passed the order while hearing an anticipatory bail petition filed by Subhash Gupta, a partner of Gupta Property Developers, Shivji, in connection with an FIR under Sections 420, 120-B and 506 of the IPC, corresponding to Sections 318(4), 61 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

In its order, the High Court had expressed serious concern over the investigation, observing that attempts had been made to shield the main accused, who are accused of cheating numerous investors of crores of rupees by collecting money for real estate projects without delivering possession or returning the invested amounts.
The High Court had noted that, despite earlier directions, the investigation had not proceeded properly.

It noted that a Special Investigation Team headed by Rohtak Superintendent of Police Gaurav Rajpurohit was investigating the case and that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan, a director of DHL Infratech Private Limited, and Gurvinder Jeet Singh, an employee of Gupta Property Developers, had been arrested.
The Court noted that Kuldeep Kumar Tahlan had been granted bail, whereas Gurvinder Jeet Singh's bail plea had been dismissed by the courts at Rohtak.

It further observed that three directors of DHL Infratech and its authorised signatory, Sidhant, had been granted interim anticipatory bail by the same presiding officer who had dismissed the bail plea of the petitioner before the High Court.

stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Law Commission To Recommend Measures For Speedy Execution Of Arbitral Awards
stories.summary: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) requested the Law Commission of India to undertake a focused study of the statutory and procedural framework governing the enforcement and execution of arbitral awards and recommend measures to ensure their timely enforcement.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh said that the prolonged execution of arbitral awards undermines the very objective of arbitration as an effective alternative to conventional civil litigation.
The Court observed that even after an award is rendered and survives judicial challenge, the successful party may be forced to undergo another prolonged round of litigation to realise its benefits.

“The promise of arbitration remains unfulfilled if a party, having traversed the arbitral process, is compelled to embark upon another protracted course of litigation to secure the benefit of the award,” the Court observed.
The judgment was passed in an appeal arising from a dispute in an international commercial arbitration between Iraq-based Royal Construction Company Pvt.
and National Projects Construction Corporation concerning the enforcement of an arbitral award rendered in 2002.
More than 24 years after the award, the parties were still litigating over its enforcement.
The Court noted that the efficacy of the arbitration regime cannot be assessed merely by the speed with which an award is rendered or the limited grounds available to challenge it.
It must also be assessed by whether the successful party can realise the fruits of the award within a reasonable time.

It observed that Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provides for the enforcement of arbitral awards in the same manner as decrees of courts, thereby relying on the ordinary execution machinery under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Court identified several aspects warranting focused scrutiny, including the identification and disclosure of the award-debtor's assets, coordination between different modes of execution, disposal of repetitive or dilatory objections, and the time taken to conclude execution proceedings.

stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Bombay High Court Ruling Setting Aside ₹8,415 Crore YES Bank AT-1 Bond Write-Down
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has dismissed appeals filed by YES Bank Limited, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Union of India, upholding the Bombay High Court's decision setting aside the permanent write-down of YES Bank's Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth ₹8,415 crore.

A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih held that the Administrator of YES Bank could not write down the bonds in contravention of the final YES Bank Limited Reconstruction Scheme, 2020, particularly when the provision expressly providing for the write-down had been omitted from the notified scheme.
The dispute arose from the Administrator's decision dated March 14, 2020, to permanently write down the AT-1 bonds following the reconstruction of the bank.
The bonds had been issued in two tranches of ₹3,000 crore and ₹5,415 crore.

The Court observed that the omission of the write-down provision from the final Reconstruction Scheme, considered alongside the deliberative process preceding its notification, indicated that the Central Government had consciously decided not to incorporate such a provision.
The Administrator could not rely on a general savings clause in the scheme to claim specific authority to write down the bonds.
The Court also examined the RBI's Basel III Capital Regulations and the Information Memoranda governing the bonds.
It considered whether the conditions authorising a write-down had been satisfied and whether the Administrator had acted in accordance with the applicable regulatory and contractual framework.
Upholding the Bombay High Court's decision, the Supreme Court held that the Administrator's action was impermissible.
The appeals were accordingly dismissed.
The Court further clarified that the annual coupon payments would remain unaffected by the outcome of the appeals and must be made in accordance with the Information Memoranda.
Dua Associates represented ECL Finance Limited, Respondent No. 14, before the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.title: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], October 28 : The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a 3 per cent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners, effective July 1, 2026, providing relief against rising prices. The move will raise DA and DR rates from the existing 60 per cent to 63 per cent of basic pay and pension, respectively. The increase is expected to benefit approximately 48.54 lakh Central Government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country. According to the government, the combined annual financial implication of the increase in DA and DR will be Rs 10,016.10 crore, adding to the Centre's expenditure. The additional instalment of DA and DR has been approved in accordance with the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. Dearness Allowance is paid to serving government employees to help offset the impact of inflation on their cost of living. Dearness Relief serves a similar purpose for pensioners, helping them manage the effect of rising prices on their pension income. The revision will be applicable retrospectively from July 1, 2026, meaning eligible employees and pensioners will be entitled to the revised rates from that date. The Cabinet's decision comes as the government continues to adjust inflation-linked benefits for its employees and pensioners through periodic revisions in DA and DR. The increase in these allowances is linked to an established formula and is intended to help protect the purchasing power of government employees and pensioners against price increases. With the latest revision, both serving employees and pensioners will receive an additional three percentage points over the previous rate of 60 per cent of basic pay or pension, respectively. The decision covers Central Government employees and pensioners and will have a combined annual impact of more than Rs 10,000 crore on the government exchequer. (ANI)

stories.headline: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.title: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.summary: Tata Motors has often looked abroad, buying foreign businesses to acquire technology, expand to new markets and accelerate ambitions that would take years to achieve at home. The track record, however, has been mixed.In 2004, it bought South Korea’s Daewoo Commercial Vehicle for about $102 million, gaining a foothold in a market where building a comparable business from scratch could have taken years, if not decades.Four years later, it made a far bolder move, paying about $2.3 billion to buy Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) from Ford Motor.Now, with its €3.9 billion acquisition of Italy’s Iveco Group, Tata Motors is returning to the familiar playbook: Buy a struggling business, leave its brand and management largely intact, and give it time.“Their acquisitions have been driven by the need to have certain technology where developing it internally could end up costing more time,” says Avik Chattopadhyay, founder of the Indian School for Design of Automobiles (INDEA) at XLRI Delhi-NCR. “It’s also about finding newer ways of doing things, of engineering and even designing your product.”Also Read: Tata Motors takes control of Iveco in €3.9 bn deal, eyes global truck marketTrack RecordTata Motors’ international acquisition strategy gathered momentum in the early 2000s, when it acquired Daewoo. The purchase gave the company access to an established South Korean truck manufacturer, its engineering capabilities and a broader product range.The next move was smaller and shows what happens when the market shrinks. Tata acquired a 21 percent stake in Spanish bus and coach manufacturer Hispano Carrocera in 2005, taking full ownership in 2009. It shut the plant four years later, saying the European bus market had suffered its worst-ever decline after the 2008 crisis.Then came JLR, an acquisition that stunned the auto industry. In 2008, when it bought the storied luxury car maker from Ford, Tata had a fledgling passenger vehicle business at home, which, only years ago, it had wanted to sell to Ford. Acquiring the British luxury car brand gave Tata access to globally recognised brands, established distribution networks, engineering centres and manufacturing facilities. It also gave the Indian company an opportunity to participate in a much higher-value segment of the automotive market.The group’s corporate structure has since changed. Tata Motors used to house its passenger and commercial vehicle (CV) businesses together. They were demerged in October 2025 and are now separately listed companies.The passenger vehicle business, which includes JLR, is now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The CV business that is buying Iveco has been branded as Tata Motors.JLR remains the most closely watched acquisition, not just because of the signal it sent about the company’s global ambitions, but also because of its striking initial turnaround.JLR lost £306 million in its first 10 months under Tata. A decade later, in 2017, it posted a pre-tax profit of £1.6 billion. Capital infusions from Tata, a stream of new models and a manufacturing facility opened in China in FY15 all helped the recovery.“We believe JLR sets a precedent for the successful integration and turnaround of Iveco, considering Iveco’s position and performance in the developed market,” Ambit said in a December 2025 report, pointing to JLR’s early success under Tata Motors as a potential model for Iveco.JLR’s early turnaround, however, proved shortlived. From 2018, the company struggled again, hit by US-China trade tensions, anxiety over Brexit and weak demand for diesel cars in Europe. It has been volatile since, reporting a loss of £244 million after tax in FY26, its first loss since FY23.Also Read: Tata Motors CV turns in profit of Rs1,254 crore; revenue surges 42 percentPlan with IvecoThe Iveco acquisition is different from JLR.JLR gave Tata access to luxury passenger vehicles, globally recognised brands and a higher-margin segment. In CVs, Tata is already a market leader in India with a market share of 36 percent in the first half of FY27. stories.headline: Can Major League Baseball hit a home run in cricket’s own country?
stories.title: Can Major League Baseball hit a home run in cricket’s own country?
stories.summary: Nick Swisher, a Major League Baseball (MLB) World Series champion and All-Star, is full of beans about his first visit to India. “The furthest I’d travelled until now is Dubai. I’m thrilled to have come this far,” says Swisher, high-fiving and bouncing his way through the media rounds, unfazed by Mumbai’s sultry October heat.While Swisher discovers India for the first time, MLB has its sights set on a much bigger prize: Growing its footprint in the country. As it looks to build momentum, the North American baseball league brought its former stars and Indian cricketers together on October 24 for the maiden edition of MLBx: A time-controlled, 3x3, mixed-gender contest.At Mumbai’s Andheri Sports Complex, on a ballpark fashioned out of a football field, Swisher turned out with fellow All-Stars Jake Arrieta and Adrian Gonzalez and 2013 World Series champion Jonny Gomes, joining cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav, among others, in teams of three, with a singular objective: To outdo one another in home runs, the sport’s most explosive and celebrated hit.This isn’t MLB’s first tango with cricket, though. In 2023, the league signed England cricketers Harry Brook and Issy Wong as its European ambassadors. Brook, a swashbuckling batter, even joined the St Louis Cardinals for a training session in Florida. But the league’s India challenge will be way tougher—it will involve making inroads into a country where cricket dominates national mindspace, and where baseball has resonated only sporadically through cultural riffs like Billy Joel’s iconic We Didn’t Start the Fire (Joe DiMaggio) or films such as Moneyball and A League of Their Own.Also Read: From Mumbai to Goa, and Jharkhand to Kerala, the growing popularity of pickleball in IndiaAccording to WPP Media’s Sporting Nation 2025 report, cricket accounted for 89 percent of the sports industry’s revenues, cornering 81 percent of sponsorship spends, 87 percent of endorsements and 95 percent of media costs. And getting a toehold in that landscape will require MLB to swing much harder than bringing India’s T20 World-Cup-winning captain Yadav on board as its first-ever Indian brand ambassador.Jeremiah Yolkut, senior vice president, global operations and events, MLB, however, sees cricket not as baseball’s rival but as its launchpad. “India has a large young population, a growing sports and entertainment market, and significant economic potential. Baseball and cricket also share fundamental similarities, which gives us a natural starting point to introduce the sport to new audiences. This is a long-term investment—we’re thinking five to 10 years ahead, not just about a single event or season,” Yolkut tells Forbes India in an emailed interview from New York. (Standing L to R) Jonny Gomes, Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Jordan Woolery, Adrian Gonzalez and Jake Arrieta; (Sitting L to R) Deepak Chahar, Jitesh Sharma, Rachel Garcia, Nick Swisher, Kashvee Gautam and Radha Yadav Photo Courtesy MLBxWith India’s sports economy at Rs1.99 lakh crore in FY26, as a recent KPMG report states, and growing at 12 to 14 percent annually, it’s no surprise that the country remains a lucrative market for foreign sports leagues. And MLB, which set up an office in New Delhi in 2019, is no exception. In seven years, Yolkut claims to have taken baseball to over 20,000 students, penetrating the grassroots through the MLB Youth Cup that now features 150 teams with 1,800 players.“But grassroots alone is only half the equation. Having an on-ground presence and school-level participation forms the bedrock of familiarity. If you want to scale in a market as dynamic as India, you have to build beyond the game,” says Vinit Karnik, managing director, content, sports & entertainment, WPP Media South Asia. And baseball knows it well enough, having taken a few swings at India earlier as well.BASEBALL’S MANY INNINGSIn 2008, Los Angeles sports agent JB Bernstein brought to India a pitching contest that was won by two Uttar Pradesh boys—Rinku Singh and Dinesh Patel. Both travelled to the US to play baseball, and their story was later turned into a biographical film in 2014, Million Dollar Arm, starring Jon Hamm. Neither eventually made it to the elite tier, making only minor league appearances, but MLB’s India connection was rekindled once again when Arjun Nimmala, a first-generation Indian-American from Florida, was selected as a top prospect for the Toronto Blue Jays in 2023. Next year, pitcher Kumar Rocker became the first player of Indian descent to debut in the league (for the Texas Rangers). Earlier this year, Maharashtrian Akshay More was signed by Japan’s Saitama Seibu Lions as a development player in the Nippon Professional League, marking another stride ahead for the sport in India.Also Read: Turning interest into fandom is our goal for women’s football: Jinisha Sharma“We’ve also invested in storytelling as well, including our Indian Baseball Dreams documentary in 2023 (on Nimmala) and the Hot Shots hitting competition in 2024, featuring cricketer Shikhar Dhawan and former MLB player Adam Jones,” says Yolkut. “That said, our strategy isn’t built around a handful of individual players. It's about developing a broader ecosystem for baseball in India.”To that end, MLB is taking a leaf out of cricket’s playbook where the ICC (International Cricket Council), its governing body, has used T20—the sport’s shortest, most exciting iteration—as a vehicle to take the game beyond its stronghold. The baseball league is following a similar script with MLBx, with a three-player, three-inning, 30-minute contest instead of the traditional nine innings. The format has already been played at 15 US venues in the past three years as well as international destinations like London (UK), Seoul (South Korea) and Mexico City (Mexico), and is set to debut in Japan (at Fukuoka) in November. Nick Swisher signs autographs for an enthusiastic crowd at the MLBx event. Photo Courtesy MLBxMLBx also borrows from the sport-plus-entertainment template popularised by the IPL (Indian Premier League), interspersing the three matches in Mumbai with DJ sets and performances by rappers Kr$na and Badshah, and setting up food kiosks as well as batting cages for fans to have a go. “It is positioned as a high-energy sports and entertainment experience. The focus is on younger, urban sports and entertainment audiences, including people discovering baseball for the first time. The pitch is about audience relevance, brand integration and the overall consumer experience—not just the sport itself,” says Nikhil Bardia, head, Rise Worldwide, the on-ground partner for MLB.Its crossover into the music and the entertainment ecosystem is evident from the fact that almost two out of three people who bought tickets for the event were buying a sports ticket on BookMyShow, the ticketing partner, for the first time. "Around half of them had previously booked a live entertainment experience with us, most often music and comedy. The audience also showed a clear willingness to pay for a premium experience, with the Lounge Hospitality tier selling out more than a week before the event and the on-field catching zone selling out entirely,” says Anil Makhija, COO-live entertainment and venues, BookMyShow. He adds that while the gameplay was at the centre, the additional touchpoints that MLBx created through food, hospitality, interactive experiences, merchandise, what have you, made the sport more accessible, encouraging participation and discovery.Globally, leagues such as the NBA have built fanbases by extending their appeal beyond the court and into fashion and lifestyle. Basketball stars—from Michael Jordan and Shaquille O’Neal to LeBron James, Kobe Bryant and Allen Iverson—have been known to sport statement outfits that have shaped popular trends. Jordan’s partnership with Nike, which began in his rookie season in 1984 and led to the launch of the Air Jordan line, arguably defined sneaker culture and continues to pay him millions in royalties. And the rise of the NBA has been intrinsically intertwined with the rise of hip-hop, with the two sharing spaces, lingo and each amplifying the aesthetics of the other.“In baseball too, the Savannah Bananas, a professional team launched in the US in 2016, has introduced a fast-paced version of the game that replaces the traditional format with entertainment, music and showmanship—just like T20 cricket. It shows how baseball is reinventing itself to make itself appealing to newer constituencies,” says Hemant Dua, founder of Inspiranti Sports and advisor to GMR Sports.Also Read: Match Ball: How Anahat Singh is fast-tracking India's Olympics dream in squashIt also proves how modern leagues must live at the intersection of sport and culture. “For a league like MLB to make a genuine dent, it needs to tap into contemporary Indian pop culture: Leveraging music, lifestyle and cross-sport appeal with icons like Yadav. When an Indian consumer sees someone they revere engaging with baseball, it creates a cultural bridge that a grassroots clinic alone cannot build,” says Karnik of WPP Media South Asia.THE LONG HAULBut how does one ensure that an event like MLBx returns for a second and third edition, and that the sport gains firmer ground in newer geographies each time? By shifting from an event mindset to a multi-layered ecosystem mindset, backed by patience, says Karnik.Touchpoints like MLBx can be hugely catalytic for baseball, while the presence of the cricketers can bring eyeballs and familiarity. But invoking similar playing mechanics—throwing a ball, hitting it with a bat and fielding it—will not necessarily translate into the growth of the sport. The experience of MLC, the franchise cricket league in the US, is a case in point: Its launch in 2023 has yet to trigger a culture shift that brings baseball fans to watch the game. “You need accessibility, viewership, grassroots and community as interconnected pillars to build an enduring sports culture,” Karnik adds.Also Read: Running is the fastest growing sporting activity in India: Anil and Vivek SinghDua, who headed MLC team Seattle Orcas until last year, confirms that cricket in the US remains largely diaspora-driven, with crossovers still minimal despite the MLC typing up with local baseball players to engender familiarity. “The one thing I can say with confidence is that whoever from baseball has come and seen T20 has been hooked. But has there been a shift in the US? I’d say no,” he says. “MLB, too, will have to go through the hard yards in India before it establishes itself here.”While MLB is looking at the IPL model, it shouldn’t expect success to come overnight. When the IPL started in 2008, cricket was already a national religion. Even then, it took years—and the convergence of cheap mobile data, rising smartphone penetration and a deliberate push towards regionality through local languages—for the league to grow into the phenomenon it is today and for its value to touch $20.6 billion (according to US-based investment bank Houlihan Lokey). “Ideally, MLB should start to build small, local connections. There is great scope that can be deeply penetrated. MLB can’t turn baseball into a full-fledged property immediately, but with MLBx, it can try and build that intensity slowly, with a lot of local anchoring,” says Saurabh Arora, chief commercial officer of IPL franchise Punjab Kings.The emergence of the Pro Kabaddi League has shown that Indian audiences have an appetite for a ‘second sport’. The league extricated kabaddi from its rural roots and relative obscurity, attracting 201 million viewers in its 11th season in 2024 and making it the most-watched sports league after the IPL and WPL (Women’s Premier League). Central to that transformation was the way the game was repackaged in a fast-paced TV-friendly format, built around a ticking clock, aimed at providing a dopamine hit—a cocktail that MLBx, too, offers. “But it's not just viewership, MLB will need participation from schools, colleges too to make the sport popular,” says Arora of Punjab Kings. “Realistically, I feel it will be a seven-to-10-year build.”What MLB needs to do in India, suggests Dua, is find that one Indian player who becomes a catalyst for the sport—much like Yao Ming, an eight-time All-Star and Hall of Famer, did for the NBA in China. The 7-foot-6 basketball star’s arrival in the NBA with the Houston Rockets in 2002 helped propel the league’s popularity in his home country, with the NBA reaching 765 million unique viewers in China by 2015, four years after Ming retired.While that number is far-fetched for MLB as of now, “even if they can get 10 to 20 million people watching in India, they would have grown an audience as good as Japan or South Korea”, Dua says. “From a population point of view, you've captured literally one country with not a lot of effort.”In the years ahead, it will be a home run as good as any.
